title: Rast wins Hockenheim Race 1 as a safety car spares him from Wittmann's undercut
dek: René Rast converted pole into victory by 1.693 seconds for Audi Sport Team Rosberg, which took the teams' title, after a safety car interrupted Marco Wittmann's undercut and the pair traded the lead.

chapters.title: A settled championship and three guests from Japan
text: The 2019 DTM season ended at the Hockenheimring on 5–6 October with most of its prizes already awarded. René Rast had clinched his second drivers' title at the Nürburgring and Audi had already secured the manufacturers' crown. What remained open was second place in the drivers' standings, between Nico Müller and Marco Wittmann, and the teams' title.

The attention of the paddock fell on three guests from Super GT, who were not eligible for points: Jenson Button in the Honda NSX-GT of Team Kunimitsu, Tsugio Matsuda in the Nismo Nissan GT-R and Ryo Hirakawa in the TOM'S Lexus LC 500, with Matsuda sharing the Nissan with Ronnie Quintarelli and Hirakawa the Lexus with Nick Cassidy. They arrived with a long list of handicaps. The DTM and Super GT had decided against any balance of performance, the guests had never used the Hankook control tyre, their cars had neither DRS nor push-to-pass, and Button said they had never made a standing start. The pit stops, with no refuelling or driver change, were new to their mechanics too. Friday's rain made it harder still, and both Cassidy and Matsuda slid off at the Sachs-Kurve.
The format gave strategy a central role: every car had to make one mandatory stop for tyres, and a stop made under a safety car would not count towards it.

chapters.title: Rast takes pole on a drying track, Button splits the Audis in sixth
text: Qualifying began on a wet track that dried steadily, and the final minutes brought a scramble for slick tyres and late improvements. Rast and Timo Glock traded the top spot before Rast held off a last rapid lap from Wittmann to take pole with 1m45.552s, the Audi driver among several to skate across the slippery run-off at the last corner. Wittmann was second, 0.127 seconds behind, and Mike Rockenfeller third, 0.231 seconds off. Glock's own final lap was spoiled by yellow flags after Loïc Duval ran into the gravel at the Sachs-Kurve, which left the BMW seventh.

The surprise was Button. After a cautious first lap on slicks the Honda driver surged up the order to sixth on 1m46.206s, 0.654 seconds from pole and the best of the Super GT cars by a distance. Jonathan Aberdein of WRT was fourth on 1m45.928s, with Duval fifth.

Robin Frijns was eighth, ahead of Sheldon van der Linde and Joel Eriksson, and Müller, the championship runner-up, could manage only eleventh on 1m46.789s. Ferdinand Habsburg was the leading Aston Martin in twelfth, while Daniel Juncadella and Jake Dennis had both taken turns on provisional pole in the wet before the track dried. Hirakawa and Matsuda filled the last two places, nearly a second and a half behind the slowest of the regular entries, Pietro Fittipaldi.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller jumps Wittmann, Glock fights a loose door
text: The weekend's first drama came before the start: Matsuda's Nissan failed to get away for the formation lap and was left stranded as the others left the grid, and Habsburg's Aston Martin had been withdrawn. Matsuda's car was repaired and sent out later, but he would not be classified.

Rast held the lead into the first corner, but Rockenfeller took second from Wittmann on the way out, and the Phoenix Audi spent the early laps as a buffer between the two title-winning rivals. Rast stretched his advantage to roughly 2.6 seconds. With Wittmann and Glock close behind Rockenfeller, the order was tight. Button lost one place at the start but stayed in the top ten.

Hirakawa dived into the pits after a single lap, the only driver to stop that early, which committed the Lexus to a second stop later. Glock, running as high as fourth, had a bigger problem: from the opening laps the driver's door on his BMW came loose, and at times he held it shut with his hand. He came in for his stop around lap ten or eleven to have it replaced, which dropped him to the back of the field.

chapters.title: The undercut that the safety car cancelled
text: The leaders came in around half distance. Wittmann pitted at the end of lap 17 to try an undercut on Rast, who came in a lap later and rejoined just ahead of the BMW on cold tyres, with Wittmann, on warmer rubber, about to pass. At that moment Philipp Eng's BMW stopped at the edge of the track, and the race director sent out the safety car on lap 19. The track marshals had reported that the car could not be pushed back, which settled the decision.

Rast kept the lead through the neutralisation, and Wittmann, who thought the undercut would have worked, was left to follow. The safety car also changed the race for those who had not yet stopped. Müller, Juncadella and Hirakawa took the chance to change tyres, but a stop under the safety car did not count as mandatory. Müller would climb to third after the restart, but he still had to take a proper stop later.
Button's stop on lap 17 had already taken 17.9 seconds, in a team still learning the routine, and sent him down to 16th. He had named pit-stop efficiency as the Super GT teams' weakness on Friday.

chapters.title: Rast counters at the hairpin and takes the team title with him
text: Racing resumed with about 20 minutes left. Rast pulled away at the restart, but Wittmann reeled him in and, on lap 25, dived inside him at the hairpin to take the lead. Rast hit back at the same corner on the next lap, running alongside Wittmann on the exit and moving back ahead before turning into the right-hander at Turn 7. Wittmann could not mount another attack, and Rast won by 1.693 seconds.

Rockenfeller completed the podium, 10.697 seconds behind, after Müller's late problems. Müller had briefly climbed to third, but he made his stop on lap 32, rejoined 16th and was sent back through the pit lane for speeding in it, finishing 17th. Frijns was fourth and Duval fifth, giving Audi four of the first five places. Glock recovered to sixth despite his door, Paul di Resta was seventh as the best Aston Martin, Bruno Spengler eighth, and Eriksson tenth.

Button was ninth, the best of the guests, after working through the pack from 16th past Jamie Green, Dennis and van der Linde. Fittipaldi spun his WRT team-mate Aberdein after the restart and drew a drive-through, and the pair finished 15th and 14th. Hirakawa was 13th, while Juncadella retired on lap 20 with a suspension problem. Rast's seventh victory of the season earned Audi Sport Team Rosberg the teams' title a race early.

facts.v: The Super GT cars raced on an unfamiliar Hankook tyre and without any balance of performance, and Button still reached ninth.

facts.t: Safety car at the wrong moment
facts.v: Wittmann pitted on lap 17 and Rast on lap 18; the safety car for Eng's stopped BMW came as Rast rejoined on cold tyres, which kept him in front.
